seoTitle: Kubernetes Pod Log Viewer: Split and Merge kubectl logs
metaDescription: Split kubectl logs output by pod and container, merge lines by timestamp and filter by pod, container or text. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Groups kubectl logs --prefix --timestamps output by pod and container and can merge all lines into one timeline.
why:
When several containers write at once, kubectl prints them in blocks. Merging by timestamp shows what happened in order across pods.

Use kubectl logs --prefix --timestamps (with --all-containers or a label selector) so each line has a [pod/name/container] tag and a time. Lines without the prefix are listed as having none.
howTo: Paste the output or choose the file.
Filter by pod, container or text.
Keep time sort on to see one timeline.

faq.a: Without it the output does not say which pod or container wrote a line.
No. It only reads text you paste.
Not directly. Use the kubectl --prefix format.
No. Parsing happens in your browser and nothing is sent. Logs can hold IP addresses and tokens, so the page does not write them into the address bar.
